claims.text: CAL FIRE's incident page for the Plaskett Fire reports that, as of September 11, 2026 at 6:31 PM, the fire (which started August 26, 2026 at 11:01 AM near Los Burros Road/Plaskett in the Los Padres National Forest, Monterey County) had burned 29,942 acres and was 83% contained, up from 79% contained the previous day; two evacuation zones have been downgraded from orders to warnings, though multiple evacuation order and warning zones remain in effect across Monterey County, and Highway 1 remains partially closed between mile marker 19 and mile marker 11.1.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Timber Fire reports that, as of September 19, 2026 at 6:22 PM, the fire had burned 25,436 acres and remained 59% contained (essentially unchanged from September 17), with 661 structures still listed as threatened; the incident is transitioning toward hold, patrol and monitor operations, with Southwest Area Incident Management Team 1 handing command to California Interagency Incident Management Team 6 on September 22, 2026.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Plaskett Fire reports that, as of September 19, 2026 at 6:24 PM, the fire had burned 30,124 acres and remained 97% contained (unchanged from September 16); crews continue patrol, mop-up and monitoring operations, addressing isolated heat sources in remaining perimeter sections.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Timber Fire reports that, as of September 11, 2026 at 6:31 PM, the fire (which started August 8, 2026 at 8:35 PM southeast of Loma Vista in the Los Padres National Forest, Monterey County) had burned 25,420 acres and was 27% contained; evacuation orders have been downgraded in portions of Big Sur and previous shelter-in-place orders have been lifted as conditions improved, though 13 areas remain under evacuation orders and 27 under evacuation warnings across Monterey County, with crews conducting suppression, mop-up and patrol operations; no injuries or deaths were reported.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Timber Fire reports that, as of September 12, 2026 at 8:02 PM, the fire had burned 25,426 acres and was 39% contained, up from 27% contained the previous day; the fire 'remains active with isolated heat in the interior and difficult-to-access portions of the fire,' with crews continuing direct suppression and mop-up operations in steep terrain, particularly in the Ventana Wilderness area.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Plaskett Fire reports that, as of September 14, 2026 at 7:18 PM, the fire had burned 29,976 acres and was 89% contained, up from 83% contained on September 11; Evacuation Orders remain in effect for zones FHL-G011, FHL-G012-B, FHL-G014, FHL-G017, FHL-G018 and FHL-G023, while Evacuation Warnings are in effect for zones MRY-G016, MRY-F033, MRY-F034, MRY-F035 and MRY-F036, in Monterey County on Los Padres National Forest land under USFS jurisdiction, managed by California Interagency Incident Management Team 7.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Timber Fire reports that, as of September 15, 2026 at 6:30 PM, the fire had burned 25,426 acres and was 44% contained, up from 39% on September 12; 661 structures remain listed as threatened, and 3 responder injuries are reported.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Plaskett Fire reports that, as of September 15, 2026 at 6:34 PM, the fire had burned 29,993 acres and remained 89% contained; the Highway 1 closure has been lifted, with Highway 1 fully reopened through the Plaskett Fire area and between Cambria and Carmel.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Plaskett Fire reports that, as of September 16, 2026 at 6:16 PM, the fire had burned 29,993 acres and reached 97% containment (up from 89%); the Monterey County Sheriff's Office has lifted all evacuation orders and warnings connected to the fire.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Timber Fire reports that, as of September 16, 2026 at 6:12 PM, the fire had burned 25,435 acres and remained 44% contained, with 661 structures still listed as threatened; evacuation orders remain in effect for 10 zones and warnings for 16 zones, with three zones downgraded from orders to warnings and thirteen zones lifted to normal status that day.

CAL FIRE's incident page for the Timber Fire reports that, as of September 17, 2026 at 5:52 PM, the fire had burned 25,435 acres and was 59% contained, up from 44% on September 16; 661 structures remain listed as threatened and 3 responder injuries are unchanged, with evacuation orders remaining in effect for 10 zones and warnings for 16 zones. Operations are transitioning toward hold, patrol and monitor status as containment strengthens and resources are consolidated.

description: The Plaskett and Timber wildfires have burned roughly 55,560 combined acres along California's Big Sur coast since August 2026. The Timber Fire ignited August 8 and the larger Plaskett Fire ignited August 26 in the Los Padres National Forest near Big Sur; CAL FIRE now reports the Plaskett Fire holding at 97% containment on 30,124 acres, with all evacuation orders and warnings previously lifted, while the Timber Fire holds at 59% containment on 25,436 acres with evacuation orders still active for 10 zones in Monterey County as command transitions to a new incident management team on September 22. No deaths have been reported by CAL FIRE for either fire, though the Timber Fire has caused 3 responder injuries.

impact.summary: CAL FIRE reports no deaths from either fire, but 3 responder injuries on the Timber Fire. As of September 19, 2026, the Plaskett Fire holds at 97% containment on 30,124 acres, with all evacuation orders and warnings previously lifted by the Monterey County Sheriff's Office. The Timber Fire holds at 59% containment on 25,436 acres, with 661 structures still threatened and evacuation orders in effect for 10 zones (warnings for 16 more), as command transitions from Southwest Area Incident Management Team 1 to California Interagency Incident Management Team 6 on September 22.
